standard-dialogue.player: Hello, Longramble. How goes the hunt for the edge of the world?

standard-dialogue.npc: Truth be told, I've found myself getting a bit side- tracked. The potential discovery of Arposandra is quite an exciting one!
Yes, that's why I've not dared go inside again. It's much safer out here. Slightly less smelly as well.

standard-dialogue.player: Slightly being the key word there.

standard-dialogue-once-after-completing-.npc: Hello there. How goes the hunt for Arposandra?

standard-dialogue-once-after-completing-.player: I think I've found an entrance to the city, but it's too well defended. There's all these traps, and some talking terrorbird guards!

standard-dialogue-once-after-completing-.npc: Talking terrorbirds? There must be some strange magic being practised in there. What do you plan to do?

standard-dialogue-once-after-completing-.player: I don't know. I think I've hit a dead end for now.

standard-dialogue-once-after-completing-.npc: That's a shame. Still, you've made a big discovery. It will be quite the tale to tell... assuming anyone believes a story about talking terrorbirds, that is.

standard-dialogue-when-delivering-a-tang.text: You hand over the tangled toads' legs to the very grateful-looking gnome. He stuffs them straight into his mouth and hands you a mint cake in return.
Longramble continues into his standard dialogue.

attempting-to-grapple-the-tree-without-a.player: I appear to have misplaced the grappling equipment I need to cross the river.

attempting-to-grapple-the-tree-without-a.npc: That wasn't very clever, was it?
Well, it's a good job explorers like me know how to use their surroundings. I have an idea!

attempting-to-grapple-the-tree-without-a.text: Longramble explains, in huge detail, a wildly complicated plan to get you across the river. It involves using various items scrounged from the local flora and fauna.

Before you know it, you find yourself on the other side of the river with a bump on your head and no recollection of how you got across. You wonder what Longramble's plan was. It must have been very clever.
